earned_by: SOFT-HUB-20261024-001C-P001 proves the arm inequality for tree gadgets of the open knots and leaves gadgets with cycles open. Scoping before this contract, disclosed: annealing for the ratio of the two sides at sizes 4 to 20 (24 seeds each, 8,000 moves) never exceeded 1 and reached exactly 1 in almost every run; chains of double edges of length 1 to 10 stayed at most 1; on 6,483 small axis-terminal cases (4,422 with cycles) linked pairs split by the empty side at the first branching knot never exceeded F(u + e_i)F(u-bar) or F(u)F(u-bar + e_i); the bound per partner solution failed in 77 cases, per image difference pattern in 131 of 42,483, one-sided path-flip matchings into the two target classes in 245 of 11,103, and the minor inequality in 7,881 of 240,000, while the arm inequality never failed. Fresh: annealing at sizes up to 40 with 48 seeds and two generators, chains up to length 12, gadgets with every non-terminal slot paired, and exact counts on 2,000 new small gadgets.
question: Does any gadget of an open knot with cycles violate the arm inequality F(u)F(u-bar) <= s_u + F(u + e_i)F(u-bar) + F(u)F(u-bar + e_i), and do linked pairs obey the split bounds by the side empty at the first branching knot?

public_inputs.knot: the open knot excluding 000, 011 and 101 (the other five are relabellings or complements)
public_inputs.gadgets: connected native networks with pins, free legs and three terminals, self-loops and parallel edges allowed, counted exactly
public_inputs.annealing: sizes 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32 and 40 knots; 48 seeds per size, even seeds with pin probability 0.3 and odd seeds 0.75 in the generator; 20,000 moves; objective the largest over the four axes and three terminals of log(lhs / rhs)
public_inputs.chains: chains of double edges: terminal 1's knot joined by two edges to a second knot, which joins by one edge to the next pair, and so on, ending in a knot carrying terminals 2 and 3; lengths 1 to 12; 300 random place orders per length
public_inputs.cores: gadgets in which every non-terminal slot lies on an internal edge, with 3, 5, ..., 15 knots; 2,000 random gadgets per size
public_inputs.pairs: 2,000 random gadgets with 2 to 7 knots and at most 13 unpinned variables, pin probability 0.3 or 0.75 alternately; for every axis with F(u)F(u-bar) at most 3,000 and every terminal i, every pair is classified

definitions: lhs = F(u)F(u-bar); rhs = s_u + F(u + e_i)F(u-bar) + F(u)F(u-bar + e_i), with s_u the split products. A linked pair has one difference component containing all three terminals; its first branching knot on terminal i's difference walk has local tuples c and c-bar; link_A counts linked pairs whose first configuration is empty there, link_B the others.

predictions.P1_no_violation_annealing: fresh at scale: no annealed gadget has lhs > rhs for any axis and terminal
predictions.P2_no_violation_families: fresh: no chain or core gadget has lhs > rhs for any axis and terminal
predictions.P3_split_bounds: fresh at scale: on every small gadget, axis and terminal, link_A <= F(u + e_i)F(u-bar) and link_B <= F(u)F(u-bar + e_i)
predictions.reported: largest lhs/rhs by part and size; the number of cases with equality; on the small gadgets, how often the bound fails per partner solution, per image difference pattern, and for the minor inequality

controls: (i) annealing restricted to tree gadgets at sizes 8 and 16 (24 seeds) never exceeds lhs/rhs = 1 (SOFT-HUB-20261024-001C-P001); (ii) the annealer reaches lhs/rhs = 1 at sizes 4, 8 and 12; (iii) the planted function [10, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 10] is flagged; (iv) on the small gadgets, separated + linked = F(u)F(u-bar) and separated <= s_u
decision_rule: If a control fails, the result is invalid. Supported if P1, P2 and P3 all hold. Refuted otherwise, naming the predictions that failed.
stop_rule: Run controls, then every part once, writing rows as they finish; decide when all parts are in. No adaptive extension.
seeds: annealing 1000 * size + seed index; chains 20261028; cores 20261029; pairs 20261030; controls 800000 and up
environment: the workspace .venv Python with numpy; pair classification with the standard library
red_team_r0: A search cannot prove the inequality; P1 and P2 holding is evidence, not a theorem.
The annealer weakens at large sizes, as seen before, so the largest sizes are weak evidence.
The split bounds are tested only on small gadgets where pairs can be enumerated.
nonclaims: No proof of the arm inequality for gadgets with cycles.
